rv.q: It's a fascinating and sometimes deeply touching play that potently evokes the atmosphere and concerns of working women in the early Thirties.

I wonder if it hasn't now gone off the boil a bit. What might have been considered to be hot and steamy then will, I fancy, seem distinctly weak and tepid to modern theatre-goers.

cn.t: Peter Nichols' adultery drama divides critics who find it technically audacious and emotionally raw, though some feel it's dated. Wanamaker's performance and the alter-ego device earn praise, but opinions split on whether it still resonates.
